hidden_data_integrity: The proxy is a strict subset of the final. ImageNetV2 matched-frequency has exactly 10,000 images (1,000 classes x 10). The proxy is offsets 0-1 (2,000 images) and the final is offsets 0-9 (all 10,000), so 20% of the final rows are proxy rows (harness/grade.py:60-61; harness/final_eval.py:15-18 'the proxy is now *inside* the final -- 2000 of the 10000 rows are the ones the Agent tuned on'; environment/assets.lock.yaml:161-174 'derived_from: data/imagenetv2_final'; declaration.py:36-37, 172-174).

Proxy labels are visible: the class directory name is the label (grade.py:68-91). The proxy is mounted in both explore and formal retrain (declaration.py:83, 109-113; assets.lock.yaml:174), so every formal recipe searches coefficients on the same 2,000 labelled rows that make up 20% of the score. The other 8,000 rows and their labels are mounted only at scoring (declaration.py:174; assets.lock.yaml:150). No case page found final-only identifiers in any trajectory.

Proxy-to-final leakage, measured from the case pages' own split diagnostics. Best artifacts score 0.001-0.003 higher on the full set than on the unseen 8,000 rows. For the uniform soup the difference is only +0.0005 (uniform: full 0.6859, proxy 0.688, unseen 0.685375). So including the proxy rows inflates each cell's gain over the baseline by about 0.0015-0.0026 top-1, typically 20-30% of the gain: sonnet-5/max 17%, luna/low 22%, opus/low 22%, terra/medium 31%. That is about 0.005-0.008 sigma per cell. In luna/high and sol/none, best-of-3 selection between checkpoints is decided entirely by proxy-overlap rows.
network_mode = 'no-network' (task.toml:32); retrain and score use --network=none (orchestrator/container.py:216-230); explore reaches only the model API (orchestrator/egress.py:1-4).

ImageNetV2 is public with a direct download URL (assets.lock.yaml:128-135), and the 72 ingredients are the public model-soups release (task.toml:44). Agents could in principle recall the published greedy-soup recipe, but nothing in the case pages suggests use, and the shipped soup.py already implements strict greedy.
scorer_issues: The artifact gate exists and is real. soup_check solves for the checkpoint's coefficients against all 72 ingredients and rejects residual/norm > max(1e-6, 10 x the honest float32 reference) (harness/soup_check.py:118-119, 301-306). A violation writes status 'invalid' with no reward (harness/final_eval.py:160-183). Every cell's artifacts passed. Extrapolative and negative coefficients are explicitly allowed (instruction.md:25).

The evaluator docstring says 'v1 takes the last checkpoint and has no selection step' (final_eval.py:9-10). The orchestrator actually takes the best of up to 3 on the final (orchestrator/final_score.py:147-150; task.toml:19). With the proxy inside the final, this adds a second selection on the scored rows. Internal documentation inconsistency.
No training: the task selects or weights frozen checkpoints (declaration.py:3-6 'There is no training loop anywhere in it'; instruction.md:25). This matches the paper.
anchor_issues: Baseline 0.686 is the shipped uniform soup (0.6859, instruction.md:36). The case pages' 'fixed start' is model_69 at 0.6874, which is above the paper baseline. Submitting the shipped best_single option therefore scores sigma 0.104 > 0.1, a 'win' that the task itself calls 'a statistical tie, not a demonstrated regression' (instruction.md:42).

Optimum 1.0 (100% ImageNetV2 top-1) is unreachable for ViT-B/32 soups. The realistic ceiling is about 0.70-0.71, so sigma = 0.1 + 0.9*(x - 0.686)/0.314 confines every result to about 0.10-0.15. The 28 scored cells span 0.6918-0.7006, i.e. sigma 0.117-0.142.

The shipped code already contains strict_greedy (solution/run.sh:29-33; solution/soup.py:63). Setting SELECTION_RULE=strict_greedy gives 0.6936 = sigma 0.122, the score of 10 of 28 scored cells to within 0.0001, just under the median (0.6939). The task's sigma mostly measures whether the agent switched on the shipped greedy rule, plus noise.
task_level.noise: Class-clustered SE on the full 10,000 rows is about 0.0067 (grade.py:120-161; case pages). Paired SE against the references is about 0.0023-0.0025 (terra/low, luna/none pages). The 28 scored configurations span 0.6918-0.7006: 0.0088 top-1, about 1.3 marginal SE or about 3.5 paired SE end-to-end. The median cluster (0.6935-0.6942, 16 cells) is separated by at most 7 images, far inside the noise. Only sol/max (0.7006), sonnet-5/max and low (0.6985/0.6983) and sol/high (0.6972) stand meaningfully above the shipped-greedy level, and their margins (0.004-0.007) are comparable to the proxy-overlap inflation (about 0.002) plus best-of-3 selection. In sigma units, all configuration differences in this task are 0.025 or less.
task_level.checkpoint_selection: Best of up to 3 on the final metric (orchestrator/final_score.py:147-150). In 12 of 28 scored cells the official checkpoint is not the last: opus/low, max, medium; sonnet/medium; kimi/max; luna/high, max, xhigh; sol/low, max, medium; terra/max. The mean gain over the last checkpoint is +0.0025 sigma per cell (0.1204 vs 0.1179); the largest are opus/low (+0.014) and opus/medium (+0.0135). No beat-the-baseline outcome flips, because every scored artifact except an exported uniform control sits at or above 0.6874. Because 20% of the final rows are proxy rows, part of this selection is selection on the proxy rows themselves (luna/high, sol/none).

task_level.summary: Model Soup does no training: agents search coefficients over 72 frozen CLIP fine-tunes. The leads are confirmed. The 2,000 proxy rows (offsets 0-1, labels visible, mounted in both exploration and formal replay) are a strict subset of the 10,000 final rows (offsets 0-9 of ImageNetV2's 10,000 images). Proxy-tuned coefficients therefore carry about 0.002 of unearned top-1 into the final, roughly 20-30% of each cell's gain over the baseline, and in two cells best-of-3 is decided purely by proxy-overlap rows. The affine-hull gate is real and the 8,000 final-only rows were not exposed. The decisive problem is the scale. The paper baseline (uniform, 0.686) sits below the stated start (model_69, 0.6874), and the optimum of 100% is unreachable, so sigma is confined to 0.10-0.15. All 28 scored cells land at 0.117-0.142, and 10 of them are within 0.0001 of the shipped strict_greedy option (0.6936, sigma 0.122). Configuration differences are inside noise and contribute at most 0.0025 to any configuration's 10-task mean. No cell is a false positive or false negative. The task's sigma does not measure the claimed capability, so we code CONSTRUCT (confirmed). It counts toward the threshold because the proxy-in-final overlap is a confirmed defect that changes every scored cell, but its absolute effect is small (about 0.006 sigma per cell; Soup is about 7% of total benchmark sigma).

cells.approach: Learned affine soup: the 72 sum-one coefficients (negatives allowed) are fit by cross-entropy distillation of a proxy-label-ranked top-K teacher ensemble, with CV and bootstrap fits. Best is the last checkpoint (proxy 0.7015, unseen 8,000 rows 0.6915).
evidence: case page: 'proxy-label ingredient ranking -> top-K mean softmax teacher -> cross-entropy/Adam -> 72 sum-one coefficients, negatives allowed'

cells.approach: Gradient-learned affine coefficients: Adam on proxy cross-entropy with a mean-gradient projection, step and shrink chosen by split-half CV. Used 3.5% of the formal budget. Official best is artifact-5 (unseen rows 0.693375), not the last (0.6911).
evidence: case page: 'Frozen CLIP proxy cross-entropy supplies Adam gradients; subtracting the mean gradient preserves the affine constraint'
